units.en: ⟦0⟧ and missions represent actions that the player can or must take, each one stored within a category. Decisions themselves are defined within ⟦1⟧ files, while categories are defined within ⟦2⟧. While it's typical to put the country's tag within the filename, it is actually irrelevant: files can take on any filename and there will be no difference in how they will be read.
Each decision must be stored within a category. Decision categories are defined within any ⟦0⟧ file. An incredibly basic decision category definition looks like the following:

A decision's name according to the currently-turned on language can be defined in any ⟦0⟧ file, taking the decision's name as key, and the decision's name with _desc added in the end as the name for the localisation key for the description. As an example, the localisation for these decisions for the English language will look like the following within any ⟦1⟧ file:
The following arguments can be used in either decisions or decision categories, usually with similar effect.

Usually, it is desirable to restrict the decision so that it might not always be possible to take, such as restricting it to a certain country. In order to do that, there are several ⟦0⟧ blocks, serving different purposes. A decision will only be available or visible if the corresponding conditions are met in both the category and the decision.

⟦0⟧ is a trigger block that checks only at the game's start or when loading a save, primarily used to restrict a decision to a country (As ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧) and/or a DLC (As ⟦3⟧). If a decision's or a category's allowed is unfulfilled, it will never appear unless it becomes true on the save being reloaded or ⟦4⟧. If left out, assumes to be always allowed. ⟦5⟧

⟦0⟧ is a trigger block that continuously checks every frame if allowed was met, required to make the decision or the entire category be visible in the decision selection screen. In case for targeted decisions, both FROM and ROOT can be checked here, but using target_trigger is recommended when possible for optimisation purposes. It is preferable to put country or DLC checks into allowed instead. ⟦1⟧

⟦0⟧ is a trigger block that continuously checks every frame if visible was met, required to be possible to actually take the decisions. If false, the decision (or, in case of categories, decisions within) will remain visible (unless set otherwise), but will be greyed out and be impossible to complete. This is applied on top of the political power cost. Applied differently for missions.

The icon is the small picture displayed to the left of decision's or category's name. Icons use sprites, defined in any ⟦0⟧ file, by default in ⟦1⟧. Within a decision or a category, it is set with ⟦2⟧. Note that the game automatically inserts either ⟦3⟧ or a ⟦4⟧, depending on whether it's in a decision or a category. As such, the example with icon_name will make it use the ⟦5⟧ sprite for decisions and the ⟦6⟧ for categories, or, other way around, to use ⟦7⟧ in a decision, it should have ⟦8⟧. However, ⟦9⟧ will also work, as the game will check the spriteType with the exact same name as well. Overall, it's to the developer's discretion whether to include ⟦10⟧/⟦11⟧ in the icon or not. Additionally, you can use triggers inside of the icon definition when it is a decision, as follows:

Priority is used to change the order in which decisions or categories are displayed from top to bottom, with a higher priority being closer to the top. By default, a decision has the priority of 1. Decision priority can be set in a short form for a static value or in a long form, similar to ⟦0⟧ formatting. ⟦0⟧ selects a specific state or several that will be highlighted. If the state is unknown, then ⟦1⟧ can be used as a trigger block instead, evaluated for every state on the map.
⟦0⟧ is the colour that the state highlighting will have before selecting the decision, from 0 to 3. If not set, it will default to a white outline.
⟦0⟧ is the colour that the state highlighting will have after selecting the decision during the timer before it gets removed, from 0 to 3. If not set, it will default to a white outline.

These can only be used within categories and cannot be used in separate decisions.

A decision category can have a picture defined in addition to its regular icon. A picture will show up to the left of the category's description, shifting it to the left. Pictures use sprites, defined in any ⟦0⟧ file, by default in ⟦1⟧. A sprite with the name of ⟦2⟧ can be set as the category's picture with ⟦3⟧. ⟦4⟧
A category must have a description defined in localisation for the picture to appear.

By default, a decision category is invisible unless there's at least one visible decision within. This isn't always helpful, as the category may display information vital for the player in its description. To override that, you can add a line consisting of ⟦0⟧ within the decision category.

A decision category can be assigned a map area, which will show up in the top of the decision list similarly to a decision. Clicking on the button will move the camera to the specified state or states, while setting the zoom level to the set amount. This is recommended to do in decision categories containing ⟦0⟧. A map area definition looks like the following:

⟦0⟧ sets a singular state that's used as the centre of the area where the camera will move. If the map area is to be dynamic, then formatting similar to ⟦1⟧ can be used, with ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ being available and mixable. ⟦5⟧ is the ⟦6⟧ key that will be used as the name of the pseudo-decision that moves the camera to the map area. ⟦7⟧ is the zoom level for the map area, set in the amount of pixels off the ground, meaning that a lower value results in it being zoomed in more. For comparison, by default, the player can change the camera zoom between 50⟦8⟧ and 3000⟦9⟧. Additionally, each of the trigger blocks defined for decisions and categories (aside from ⟦10⟧) can go inside of ⟦11⟧, such as ⟦12⟧.

A decision category can be set to have a scripted graphical user interface container within the category, showing up below the description. The scripted GUI in question must have the decision_category context type for this to work. This is set with ⟦0⟧. See details on the ⟦1⟧.
These can only be used within decisions and cannot be used in categories.
⟦0⟧ is the block of ⟦1⟧ that gets executed immediately when the decision is selected (Starting the timer if it has one).
By default, a decision reappears on the very next day after being taken. In order to increase the cooldown in days, ⟦0⟧ can be used to put in more days in the cooldown.
In order to make the decision disappear forever upon being completed, the ⟦0⟧ line of code will ensure that, making the decision only be possible to fire once per country.

A custom cost will not actually cost anything

As the custom cost can't be used in conjunction with the regular cost, if it includes political power, the AI will not be aware that it should save up an amount of it before taking the decision. This can be remidified with ⟦0⟧: this attribute will make the AI think that the decision will use 100 political power regardless of whether it does or not, making sure it will save up that much before trying to use it. This must be a constant amount rather than being a variable.

In order to add a timer between the decision being selected and some of its effects applying, ⟦0⟧ is used to define the amount of days. If set to ⟦1⟧, the decision will never be removed by the timer running out, although additional trigger blocks can remove it.

As for defining the effects that would be executed when the timer ends, ⟦0⟧ is used as an effect block. Note that ⟦1⟧ is when the decision is selected starting the timer, rather than when the timer ends. In other words, this timer appears after the decision was completed and stays there until the decision is removed. Additionally, ⟦2⟧ is used to instantly remove the decision once the triggers within are met for the country, also firing the ⟦3⟧ block.

Additionally, it is possible to make the decision apply ⟦0⟧ during the timer's duration, with the ⟦1⟧ providing a modifier block. ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ also exists as a way to apply ⟦4⟧, in the same formatting with ⟦5⟧ setting the target, such as the following example:

In order to make the timer cancel early without providing the effects, ⟦0⟧ does not work by default. Instead, ⟦1⟧ is used as a trigger block. Upon it being evaluated as true, the decision timer ends without ⟦2⟧ being executed. ⟦3⟧, false by default, serves as an easy way to add visible's triggers into the ⟦4⟧ block. Upon the decision being cancelled, ⟦5⟧ is an effect block that gets executed. This can be useful as a way to reverse the effects applied within the complete effect.

The chance for AI to pick a decision is decided by the ⟦0⟧ block within a decision, which is a ⟦1⟧. ⟦2⟧ and that block is required to make AI choose it.
By default, a decision will never be chosen by AI,

As a ⟦0⟧, the structure consists of ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧ to choose the initial value and ⟦3⟧ as trigger blocks assigning ⟦4⟧/⟦5⟧/⟦6⟧ in the order. For example, the following will make the decision be never chosen by AI, unless the country is at war with ITA, in which case it has 10 weight:

If your decision leads to a nation declaring war on another nation, there are several arguments that can be used to inform the targeted nation that a war is coming, as well as alert the AI to begin moving troops onto the border: ⟦0⟧ will make the game assume that the decision, within its ⟦1⟧ will declare war on the specified country, making it prepare when the timer starts. ⟦2⟧ will make the game assume that the decision, within its ⟦3⟧ will declare war on the specified country, making it prepare when the decision becomes available.
These arguments do not work for targeted decisions; see ⟦0⟧.

Decisions, by default, use a fixed random seed. What this means is that such scopes as ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ will pick the same thing each time that the decision is used, making a choice when the game starts. ⟦2⟧ will make sure that the random seed is dynamic, making it possible for a different outcome to happen.
QAT_category and BHR_category are assumed to already have been created within any ⟦0⟧ file.

Missions are another type of decisions, activated when the triggers are true and requiring the player to do an action in order for the mission to have a positive outcome. These mostly use the same attributes as regular decisions, but there are some crucial differences. In particular:
⟦0⟧ is the amount of days that the mission will last for and is the attribute that turns a decision into a mission.
⟦0⟧ are the effects that will be executed for the country if the timer runs out or is uninterrupted.
⟦0⟧ decides on triggers that make the mission possible to select, executing ⟦1⟧. ⟦2⟧.
